courses.title: Advanced Python
courses.why: Joe Marini's current advanced course: special methods, iterators and sequences, string processing, exceptions and writing efficient code, with CoderPad code challenges. It maps closely onto the Python chapters' data-model and iterator questions.

courses.title: Advanced Python: Classes and Functions
courses.why: Classes that behave like built-in types, readable functions and structural pattern matching: the OOP and functions material interviewers probe at senior level, in a short course with GitHub Codespaces exercises.

courses.title: Asynchronous Python: Boost Performance and Efficiency for Real-World Apps
courses.why: Older (2021) but only an hour, and it applies asyncio to real services (aiohttp, Redis, ASGI). Take it if the concurrency chapter felt shaky; skip it otherwise.

portals.name: Exercism: Python track
portals.what: 146 exercises across 17 concepts, with optional human mentoring on your solutions. Free.

portals.name: HackerRank: Python practice
portals.what: Short graded problems by topic (collections, itertools, closures and decorators, classes, regex), the same platform as the HackerRank Python certificate.

portals.name: roadmap.sh: Python interview questions
portals.what: 20 common questions from basics to advanced concepts, with short answers to compare against yours.

portals.name: GeeksforGeeks: Python interview questions
portals.what: 68 questions with answers and code; useful as a fast self-check before a screening call.

portals.name: The Python Tutorial (official)
portals.what: The official tutorial for the current release; the authoritative place to confirm any language detail.

assessments.name: HackerRank Python (Basic) certificate
assessments.format: 90-minute online test, 2 coding problems; retake allowed after 30 days
assessments.credential: Shareable HackerRank certificate URL for LinkedIn and your resume
assessments.why: The quickest Python credential to earn and show, and the same certificate format as your Frontend Developer (React) certificate.

assessments.name: PCAP – Certified Associate Python Programmer (PCAP-31-03)
assessments.format: 40 questions in 65 minutes, 70% to pass; Pearson VUE test centre, OnVUE online proctoring, or OpenEDG TestNow. An updated exam version (PCAP-31-04) is scheduled for release on 31 October 2026; the certification itself stays the same.
assessments.credential: Digital certificate with verification code and a Credly badge, valid for 5 years
assessments.why: The recognised vendor-neutral Python certification at the right level for an experienced developer: modules and packages, exceptions, strings and OOP.

assessments.name: PCPP1 – Certified Professional Python Programmer Level 1 (PCPP-32-101)
assessments.format: 45 questions in 65 minutes, 70% to pass; Pearson VUE or OnVUE online proctoring
assessments.credential: Professional-level certificate and badge (lifetime validity for PCPP-32-101)
assessments.why: The professional tier: advanced OOP (decorators, metaclasses, serialisation), PEP 8 and PEP 257, network programming and file processing. The most prestigious Python-only credential; take it after PCAP.
